# Sort data in the code representation of a data model

You can sort data in a table when [creating or managing a data model as code](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/manage-data-models-as-code) using the `sort` array in the table element.

By specifying how data is sorted, you can control how tables created using the [Create a data model from a code representation](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/reference/createdatamodelspec) endpoint are presented to users in the UI. This allows you to programmatically create tables according to common user needs, such as presenting data in reverse-chronological order.

## Example representation with sorted columns

The following example shows a JSON representation of a data model with a table that has an ascending sort order applied to the columns `START_DATE` and `DURATION`. This produces a table with rows sorted first by `START_DATE` with the earliest dates first. For any rows with the same `START_DATE`, they are sorted by `DURATION` in ascending order. For more information on sorting data in the Sigma UI, see [Customize the sort order of table elements](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/configure-custom-sort#customize-the-sort-order-of-a-table).

<Accordion title="Full JSON representation with sort">
  ```json
  {

    "name": "sort",
    "url": "https://aws-api.sigmacomputing.com/org-name/data-model/sort-JDEWh0IJtkmfpYrf6NEg9",
    "documentVersion": 2,
    "latestDocumentVersion": 2,
  ```

## Representing sort order

In this representation, the sort order is specified in the `sort` array of the table element. The `sort` array contains objects that define which columns to sort by and in what direction. In this example, there is a custom sort applied to the table that sorts first by `START_DATE` in ascending order, and then by `DURATION` in ascending order. Both place `null` values last in the order.

<Accordion title="Sort representation">
  ```json
  ...
  "sort": [
    {
      "columnId": "inode-8msHptIwZ86qB4JPcIdql8/START_DATE",
      "direction": "ascending",
      "nulls": "last"
    },
    {
      "columnId": "inode-8msHptIwZ86qB4JPcIdql8/DURATION",
      "direction": "ascending",
      "nulls": "last"
    }
  ]
  ...
  ```
</Accordion>

# Specify column order in the code representation of a data model

You can specify order of columns in a table when [managing data models as code](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/manage-data-models-as-code) using the `order` array in the table element.

By specifying column order, you can control how tables created using the [Create a data model from a code representation](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/reference/createdatamodelspec) endpoint are presented to users in the UI, allowing you to logically sequence columns left-to-right based on their contents, data types, usage, and more.

## Representing order

In this representation, the column order is specified in the `order` array of the table element. The `order` array contains the IDs of the columns and folders in a table in the order you want them to appear in the table, where the first item in the `order` array is the left-most column in the Sigma UI.

<Accordion title="Order representation">
  ```json
  ...
  "order": [
    "6dLyS0e3wh",
    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/AIRLINE",

    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/TAIL_NUMBER",

    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/SCHEDULED_DEPARTURE",
    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/DEPARTURE_TIME",
    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/DEPARTURE_DELAY",
    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/TAXI_OUT",
    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/WHEELS_OFF",
    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/SCHEDULED_TIME",
    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/ELAPSED_TIME",
    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/AIR_TIME",
    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/DISTANCE",
    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/WHEELS_ON",
    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/TAXI_IN",
    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/SCHEDULED_ARRIVAL",
    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/ARRIVAL_TIME",
    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/ARRIVAL_DELAY",
    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/DIVERTED",
    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/CANCELLED",

    "inode-Ayhp5bdwjOj7J3rwU39F9y/WEATHER_DELAY"

  ...
  ```
</Accordion>

Here, entries formatted as short alphanumeric IDs, such as `6dLyS0e3wh`, identify either a folder of multiple columns or a calculated column. Entries formatted as `inode-<id>/<column_name>` are individual columns from the table source.

# Update a data model from a code representation

Source: https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/update-a-data-model-from-a-code-representation.md

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://help.sigmacomputing.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Update a data model from a code representation

You can update an existing data model from a code representation by calling the [Update a data model from a representation](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/reference/updatedatamodelspec) endpoint with the code representation in the request body.

This document provides step-by-step instructions for using this endpoint to update a data model from a code representation. For more information on working with data models programmatically, see [Manage data models as code](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/manage-data-models-as-code).

## System and user requirements

The ability to update a data model from a code representation requires the following:

* You must have developer credentials for the Sigma API. For more information, see [Get started with the Sigma REST API](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/reference/get-started-sigma-api).
* The user associated with your API credentials must be assigned an [account type](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/create-and-manage-account-types) with the **Create, edit, and publish data models** permission enabled.
* You must be the document owner or be granted **Can edit** [access](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/folder-and-document-permissions) to the data model.

## Generate API client credentials and an API access token

To start, you must generate credentials for the Sigma API. These credentials are used to retrieve an access token, which is required to make requests to the API.

For step-by-step instructions on generating developer credentials in Sigma and using them to authenticate to the Sigma API, see the instructions in [Generate client credentials](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/reference/generate-client-credentials).

## Identify the data model and retrieve the data model ID

To update an existing data model from a code representation, you must know the unique `dataModelId` for that data model. When you have identified the data model you want to update the representation for, you can call the [List data models](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/reference/listdatamodels) endpoint to retrieve the `dataModelId`:

1. Go to your **Home** page.

2. In the navigation menu, select **My documents**.

3. Click the **Document type** ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/caret.svg) filter and select **Data models**.

   The list of your data models appears.

4. Identify the data model you want to update the representation for, by name, owner, or other details.

5. Make a GET request to the [List data models](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/reference/listdatamodels) endpoint like the following:

   <Accordion title="List data models request format">
     ```shell
     curl --request GET \
          --url <base_url>/v2/dataModels \
          --header 'Authorization: Bearer <access_token>' \
          --header 'accept:application/json' \
          --header 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
     ```
   </Accordion>

The response includes a list of data models in your organization, in the following format:

<Accordion title="List data models response format">
  ```json
  {
    "entries":
      [
        {
          "dataModelId": "<dataModelId>",
          "dataModelUrlId": "<dataModelUrlId>",
          "createdBy": "<userId>",
          "updatedBy": "<userId>",
          "createdAt": "<timestamp>",
          "updatedAt": "<timestamp>",
          "name": "<dataModelName>",
          "url": "<dataModelUrl>",
          "path": "<folderPath>",
          "latestVersion": "<versionNumber>",
          "ownerId": "<userId>"
        },
        {
          "dataModelId": "<dataModelId>",
          "dataModelUrlId": "<dataModelUrlId>",
          "createdBy": "<userId>",
          "updatedBy": "<userId>",
          "createdAt": "<timestamp>",
          "updatedAt": "<timestamp>",
          "name": "<dataModelName>",
          "url": "<dataModelUrl>",
          "path": "<folderPath>",
          "latestVersion": "<versionNumber>",
          "ownerId": "<userId>"
        }
      ],
    "hasMore": <boolean>,
    "total": <number>,
    "nextPage": null
  }
  ```
</Accordion>

6. Identify the data model you want to update the representation for, and copy the `dataModelId` to pass to the [Update a data model from a representation](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/reference/updatedatamodelspec) endpoint.

## Prepare the representation

To update an existing data model from a code representation, you must prepare a valid code representation of the data model with the updates you want to apply. You can base this on the representation of the existing data model, or update the data model using an entirely new representation.

<Callout icon="💡" theme="default">
  The [Update a data model from a representation](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/reference/updatedatamodelspec) endpoint supports PUT requests, and does not support partial updates. To update a data model, you must pass in a complete representation of the data model, even if you are only making minor changes. Sigma recommends retrieving the existing representation and basing your changes on that.
</Callout>

The code representation you prepare can be passed into the request body of the [Update a data model from a representation](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/reference/updatedatamodelspec) endpoint to update the data model.

1. Using the `dataModelId` you identified in the previous section, follow the instructions in [Retrieve the code representation](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/get-the-code-representation-of-a-data-model#retrieve-the-representation) to get the current representation.

## Call the Update a data model from a code representation endpoint

Finally, call the [Update a data model from a code representation](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/reference/updatedatamodelspec) endpoint, passing the `dataModelId` as a path parameter and the updated code representation in the request body. The request format is as follows:

<Accordion title="Update a data model from a representation request format">
  ```shell
  curl --request PUT \
      --url <base_url>/v2/dataModels/<dataModelId>/spec \
      --header 'Authorization: Bearer <access_token>' \
      --header 'content-type:application/json' \
      --data '<json_representation>'
  ```
</Accordion>

This example request replaces the example representation shown after step one of the previous section with the truncated representation from step two:

<Accordion title="Update a data model from a representation request example">
  ```shell
  curl --request PUT \                               
      --url https://aws-api.sigmacomputing.com/v2/dataModels/575ba1f9-7c5d-4cf0-83df-9a0bea884b8d/spec \
      --header 'Authorization: Bearer <access_token>' \
      --header 'content-type:application/json' \
      --data '{"dataModelId":"467bc369-5db7-4963-8172-b24a49dbc75b","name":"Plugs Orders","url":"https://aws-api.sigmacomputing.com/org-name/data-model/Plugs-Orders-ZwGvRngQvdGnD3FLar3PMD","documentVersion":2,"latestDocumentVersion":2,"schemaVersion":1,"ownerId":"Gm0tRQp8R91nfN7nhZ1RnXyhAFbGm","folderId":"21c662bd-d01e-4b2a-b6c9-559670a79a1d","createdBy":"Gm0tRQp8R91nfN7nhZ1RnXyhAFbGm","updatedBy":"Gm0tRQp8R91nfN7nhZ1RnXyhAFbGm","createdAt":"2025-11-17T20:30:10.664Z","updatedAt":"2025-11-17T20:31:30.158Z","pages":[{"id":"baXffaLXOI","name":"Page 1","elements":[{"id":"4djgrzPSow","name":"PLUGS_ELECTRONICS_HANDS_ON_LAB_DATA","kind":"table","source":{"connectionId":"d61d33dd-3f3b-4cf6-bb08-d7e5bf0136ac","kind":"warehouse-table","path":["EXAMPLES","PLUGS_ELECTRONICS","PLUGS_ELECTRONICS_HANDS_ON_LAB_DATA"]},"columns":[{"id":"inode-5FCsrDpnzcdw5YYJRBbY6l/ORDER_NUMBER","name":"Order Number","formula":"[PLUGS_ELECTRONICS_HANDS_ON_LAB_DATA/Order Number]"},{"id":"inode-5FCsrDpnzcdw5YYJRBbY6l/DATE","name":"Date","formula":"[PLUGS_ELECTRONICS_HANDS_ON_LAB_DATA/Date]"}]}]}]}'
  ```

The data model is updated with the new representation.

# Sigma CLI

You can work programmatically in Sigma using the Sigma command-line interface (CLI) tool. The Sigma CLI (`sigcli`) simplifies interaction with the Sigma REST API by providing quality-of-life features to developers, such as authentication management, typed commands, and profile-based configuration.

<Callout icon="🚩" theme="default">
  The Sigma CLI is an external command line interface tool, the use of which is governed by the CLI license. Review the [Sigma CLI Notice](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/notice-for-sigma-cli-license) before using the Sigma CLI to connect with or access your Sigma organization.
</Callout>

You can use the Sigma CLI to:

* Automate the management of connections, users, and documents in Sigma
* Integrate Sigma operations into CI/CD pipelines and scripts
* Query and export data programmatically
* Simplify requests to the Sigma REST API for users and AI assistants

For instructions on how to get started with the Sigma CLI, see [Install and configure the Sigma CLI](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/install-and-configure-the-sigma-cli). For information on using the Sigma CLI, see [Use the Sigma CLI](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/use-the-sigma-cli).

# Install and configure the Sigma CLI

Source: https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/install-and-configure-the-sigma-cli.md

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://help.sigmacomputing.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Install and configure the Sigma CLI

To use the Sigma CLI, you must install it on your machine. After installation, you can configure authentication, profiles, and more to manage your usage of the Sigma REST API.

<Callout icon="🚩" theme="default">
  The Sigma CLI is an external command line interface tool, the use of which is governed by the CLI license. Review the [Sigma CLI Notice](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/notice-for-sigma-cli-license) before using the Sigma CLI to connect with or access your Sigma organization.
</Callout>

## System and user requirements

Installing the Sigma CLI requires the following:

* A compatible macOS, Linux, or Windows operating system
* Internet access
* To install the Sigma CLI using Homebrew, you must install <a href="https://brew.sh/" target="_blank">Homebrew</a>
* To generate API client credentials, you must be assigned the **Admin** account type
* To authenticate a profile for the Sigma CLI with OAuth, you must be assigned an [account type](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/user-account-types) with the **Use Sigma API with OAuth** permission enabled

## Install the Sigma CLI

You can install the Sigma CLI using the provided shell installer or using <a href="https://brew.sh/" target="_blank">Homebrew</a>.

### Shell installer

The Sigma CLI shell installer downloads and installs the latest release binary for your platform.

To install the Sigma CLI using the shell installer, run the following command:

```shell
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://assets.sigmacomputing.com/sigcli/releases/latest/sigcli-installer.sh | sh
```

The binary installs to `~/.sigcli/bin/sigcli`.

### Homebrew

To install the Sigma CLI using Homebrew, run the following command:

```shell
brew install sigmacomputing/tap/sigcli
```

The binary installs to the Homebrew `bin/` directory and is automatically added to your PATH.

### Add the Sigma CLI to your PATH

If the Sigma CLI is not automatically added to your PATH after installation, you can add the install directory to your shell profile manually:

1. In your shell profile (`~/.zshrc` for Zsh or `~/.bashrc` for Bash), add the following:

   ```shell
   export PATH="$HOME/.sigcli/bin:$PATH"
   ```

2. After saving the file, restart your shell.

The Sigma CLI becomes available in your shell session as `sigcli`.

### Verify installation

To confirm the Sigma CLI is installed and accessible, run the following command:

```shell
sigcli --version
```

If the command returns a version number, such as `0.1.1`, the Sigma CLI is installed.

## Configure a profile in the Sigma CLI

To manage multiple sets of credentials, such as when separating production and staging access, you can configure profiles in the Sigma CLI using either OAuth or API client credentials.

### Configure a profile using OAuth

To configure a profile for the Sigma CLI using OAuth, create a profile and log in to your Sigma organization:

1. Run the login command:

   ```shell
   sigcli auth login
   ```

2. Select **Create new profile**.

3. For **Authentication method**, select **OAuth**.

4. Enter the URL for your Sigma organization. For example, `https://app.sigmacomputing.com/example-organization`.

5. Enter a name for the new profile. For example, `staging`.

6. A new browser tab opens, prompting you to sign in to your Sigma organization. Sign in, then return to the terminal.

The profile is created in the Sigma CLI. You can authenticate to the Sigma REST API using the credentials securely stored in the profile.

To run Sigma CLI commands using the credentials stored in a profile, add `-p <profile-name>` to the command. For example, to check the authentication status of the `staging` profile, run the following command:

```shell
sigcli -p staging auth status
```

### Configure a profile using API client credentials

To configure a profile for the Sigma CLI using Sigma REST API client credentials, create a profile and add your credentials to it:

1. Identify the base URL for your Sigma organization and generate client credentials by following the steps in [Generate client credentials](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/reference/generate-client-credentials).

2. Run the login command:

   ```shell
   sigcli auth login
   ```

3. Select **Create new profile**.

4. For **Authentication method**, select **API key**.

5. Enter a name for the new profile. For example, `staging`.

6. Select the API base URL you identified in step 1.

7. Enter the credentials you generated in step 1.

The profile is created in the Sigma CLI. You can authenticate to the Sigma REST API using the credentials securely stored in the profile.

To run Sigma CLI commands using the credentials stored in a profile, add `-p <profile-name>` to the command. For example, to check the authentication status of the `staging` profile, run the following command:

```shell
sigcli -p staging auth status
```

### Verify authentication and user

After configuring multiple profiles and credentials in the Sigma CLI, you can verify authentication and identity details using the following commands:

To check the status of your current credentials, run the following command:

```shell
sigcli auth status
```

To print the current bearer token, run the following command:

```shell
sigcli auth token
```

To confirm which user is authenticated, run the following command:

```shell
sigcli api whoami get
```

# Use the Sigma CLI

Source: https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/use-the-sigma-cli.md

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://help.sigmacomputing.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Use the Sigma CLI

You can programmatically manage your Sigma documents, users, and data using the Sigma CLI. For instructions to set up the Sigma CLI, see [Install and configure the Sigma CLI](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/install-and-configure-the-sigma-cli).

This document explains the basic command structure of the Sigma CLI, outputs, and logging.

<Callout icon="🚩" theme="default">
  The Sigma CLI is an external command line interface tool, the use of which is governed by the CLI license. Review the [Sigma CLI Notice](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/notice-for-sigma-cli-license) before using the Sigma CLI to connect with or access your Sigma organization.
</Callout>

## Command structure

Commands in the Sigma CLI follow a common structure, in the format:

```shell
sigcli api <resource> <action> [--flags]
```

For example, the following command lists workbooks in the organization associated with the current profile:

```shell
sigcli api workbooks list
```

<Callout icon="📘" theme="info">
  Because the Sigma CLI is a command-line tool for the Sigma REST API, resources and actions are derived from Sigma REST API endpoints. For example, the command `sigcli api workbooks list` calls the [List workbooks](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/reference/listworkbooks) endpoint. For more information on available resources and actions, review the available endpoints in the [Sigma API reference documentation](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/reference/get-started-sigma-api).
</Callout>

To see a list of all resources you can interact with via the Sigma CLI, run the following command:

```shell
sigcli --help
```

To see a list of actions and flags for a particular `resource` type, run the following command:

```shell
sigcli api <resource> --help
```

For example, to see all actions and flags for connections, run the following command:

```shell
sigcli api connections --help
```

### Structure API calls using the Sigma CLI

To see the parameters a command accepts, including each parameter name and whether it's required, run the `schema` command for that command path:

```shell
# Print the schema for the workbooks get command
sigcli api schema workbooks get
```

To pass a path parameter, include it as a key in the JSON object you provide to the `--params` flag. For example, the [Get a workbook](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/reference/getworkbook) endpoint requires a `workbookId` path parameter:

```shell
# Retrieve a single workbook by its ID
sigcli api workbooks get --params '{"workbookId":"<workbook-id>"}'
```

To pass query parameters, add them as additional keys. For example, you can limit the number of results the [List workbooks](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/reference/listworkbooks) endpoint returns:

```shell
# List workbooks, returning at most two results
sigcli api workbooks list --params '{"limit":2}'
```

You can combine path and query parameters in the same JSON object. For example, the following command lists the pages of a specific workbook and limits the results:

```shell
# List up to three pages of a specific workbook
sigcli api workbooks pages list --params '{"workbookId":"<workbook-id>","limit":3}'
```

## Manage command output

You can pipe command output from the Sigma CLI to other commands to create custom scripts and workflows.

All command output in the Sigma CLI is formatted as JSON printed to `stdout`.

For example, to filter a list of workbooks using `jq`, run the following command:

```shell
# Pipe to jq for filtering
sigcli api workbooks list | jq '.entries[].name'
```

To save the metadata for a workbook to a file titled `workbook.json`, run the following command:

```shell
# Save to a file
sigcli api workbooks get --params '{"workbookId":"<workbook-id>"}' > workbook.json
```

## Interpret exit codes and manage errors

To check if a Sigma CLI command was successful, or to understand the cause of an error when using the Sigma CLI, refer to the following exit codes:

| Exit code | Meaning                      |
| --------- | ---------------------------- |
| `0`       | Success                      |
| `1`       | API error (HTTP 4xx/5xx)     |
| `2`       | Authentication error         |
| `3`       | Validation error (bad input) |
| `4`       | HTTP/network error           |

All errors are formatted as JSON printed to `stdout`, with a colored label printed to `stderr`.

For example, if you request a workbook with an invalid `workbookId`, such as in the following command:

```shell
sigcli api workbooks get --params '{"workbookId":"invalid-id"}'
```

The following structured error prints to `stdout`:

```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "error": "api",
  "message": "Expecting UUID at workbookId but instead got: \"inva...\"",
  "requestId": null
}
```

The error label prints to `stderr`:

```shell
error[api]: Expecting UUID at workbookId but instead got: "inva..."
```

## Enable debug logging

To troubleshoot errors when working with the Sigma CLI, you can enable debug logging by setting the `SIGCLI_LOG` environment variable.

For example, to see the debug log when requesting a list of connections, run the following command:

```shell
SIGCLI_LOG=debug sigcli api connections list
```

# Add elements and data to a report

Source: https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/add-elements-and-data-to-a-report.md

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://help.sigmacomputing.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Add elements and data to a report

Once you have [created a report](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/create-and-edit-reports), you can add elements and data to start building out your report. After adding data, you may also want to paginate table elements for ease of use and understanding. This document covers how to add elements to your report, and paginate tables and pivot tables.

Once you have added elements to your report, you may want to further customize element size and formatting. See [Customize report settings and themes](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/customize-report-elements-settings-and-branding). For more information on reports in general, see [Reports overview](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/reports-overview).

## User requirements

* To add elements to a report, you must be assigned an [account type](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/doc/license-and-account-type-overview) with **Create, edit, and publish reports** permission. See [Account type and license overview](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/doc/account-type-and-license-overview).
* You must be in **Edit** mode.

## Add elements and data to a report

Each report page provides a canvas on which you can add and arrange elements. You can add a variety of different element types:

* Data elements, like tables, charts, and pivot tables. See [Create a data element](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/create-a-data-element).
* Input elements, like empty or linked input tables. See [Intro to input tables](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/intro-to-input-tables).
* Control elements, like filters and inputs. See [Intro to control elements](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/intro-to-control-elements).
* UI elements, like text, images, embeds, dividers and page numbers. See [Intro to UI elements](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/intro-to-ui-elements) and [Edit page order, visibility, and numbers](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/edit-report-page-order-visibility-and-numbers).

Once you have added elements to a report, you can format them to meet your reporting and branding needs. See [Format report elements, themes and branding](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/customize-report-elements-settings-and-branding).

## Paginate or collapse data tables in a report

Make your data easier to navigate by paginating table and pivot tables. There are two ways to paginate data tables:

**From the table element**:

1. Select your desired table.
2. At the lower right corner of the table, select **Expand table**.
3. To collapse the table, select **Collapse table**.

**From the editor panel**:

1. Select your desired table.
2. In the **Format** tab of the editor panel, open the **Size** section, then select **Expand table rows**.
3. To collapse the table, unselect the **Expand table rows** checkbox.

### Pagination limitations

* Tables and input tables can be paginated up to 10,000 rows:
  * This limitation applies to how many rows are rendered in the report. All operations (like filtering, formulas, summaries, and any child element interactions) are performed on the entire dataset.
  * Report exports will display up to 10,000 rows of data per table/input table.
* Only vertical pagination of data tables is available. Horizontal pagination is not supported.

# Create and edit reports

Source: https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/create-and-edit-reports.md

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://help.sigmacomputing.com/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Create and edit reports

Reports are a Sigma document type designed to help you create predictable, pixel-perfect PDF exports. Precisely formatted exports are helpful for a variety of enterprise reporting needs, such as compliance, external reporting, and embedded analytics. For more information about reports, see [Reports overview](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/reports-overview).

Creating a report in Sigma allows you to [add](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/add-elements-and-data-to-a-report) and [arrange elements](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/customize-element-size-position-and-layering), manage your report [page setup](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/edit-report-page-setup-headers-and-footers) and [page order, visibility, and numbers](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/edit-report-page-order-visibility-and-numbers), [customize your report branding](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/customize-report-elements-settings-and-branding), [export reports](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/share-and-export-reports), and more.

## User requirements

* To create a report, you must be assigned an [account type](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/license-and-account-type-overview) with **Create, edit, and publish reports** permission. See [Account type and license overview](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/account-type-and-license-overview).

## Considerations when creating reports versus workbooks

Reports allow you to customize element formatting and positioning at the pixel level. When building reports, exports are always reliably formatted, helping you fully meet compliance and branding needs. If you have a clear idea of the type of analysis you want to do, and need to export your analysis for external consumers, a report is likely suitable for your needs.

However, some workbook functionality is not available in reports:

* Configuring [interactivity and actions](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/intro-to-actions) is not supported.
* Using [custom views](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/create-and-interact-with-custom-views) for ad hoc exploration is not supported.

If you want to use this functionality, and have more exploratory or heavily analytical needs that don't require precisely formatted exports, a workbook is likely more suitable.

## Create a report

You can create a report from **Home** or from an existing report:

### Create a report from the Sigma home page

1. From **Home**, select ![](https://sigma-doc-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/button-add.svg) **Create New**, then select **Report**. A new draft report is created.
2. After making your changes, select **Publish**.

Once you have created a report, you can search for it via ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/search.svg) **Search**. You can search for both draft and published reports. Unlike workbooks, there is no concept of “explorations” in reports, so unsaved reports will not appear in the **Explorations** tab of the **Recents** page.

### Create a report from an existing report

1. From an existing report, open the document menu.
2. Select **File**, then **Save** as a new report.
3. Enter a **Name** for the report, then select **Save**.

## Edit and publish a report

### Edit a report

To make changes to a report, select **Edit** in the report header.

Once you are in **Edit** mode, the **Add element** bar, toolbar, editor panel, page previews, and other functionality become available to use. Changes you make to a report draft automatically save to the live draft shared by all users who can edit the report.

### Publish a report

To publish your edits, select **Publish** in the report header. This action publishes all drafted changes to the report, including changes made by other editors using the live draft.

<Callout icon="📘" theme="default">
  When viewing the published version of a report, all users who are able to view and edit the report are able to update control values. This is the only interactivity available on a published report. Unlike when viewing a workbook, they are not able to make any other changes to the report, like updating filters, refreshing data, or creating custom and saved views.
</Callout>

# Customize element size, layering, and alignment in reports

# Customize element size, layering, and alignment in reports

You can customize the layout of your report by rearranging, resizing, layering, and aligning elements. This document covers how to [change element size and position](#change-element-size-and-position), change the [layering of your elements](#change-element-layering), and adjust the [distribution and alignment of elements](#align-and-distribute-elements).

For more information about customizing element background and style (such as corner shape or padding), see [Customize element background and styles](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/customize-element-background-and-styles). For more information on reports in general, see [Reports overview](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/reports-overview).

## User requirements

* You must be assigned an [account type](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/license-and-account-type-overview) with **Create, edit, and publish reports** permission. See [Account type and license overview](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/account-type-and-license-overview).
* You must enter **Edit** mode to configure the following.

## Change element size and position

You can edit element size and position at the pixel level to meet design and compliance requirements.

### Resize elements

There are two ways to resize elements:

* **Specify dimension in pixels**: Select the element, then select the **Format** tab in the editor panel. In the **Size** section, enter your desired **Width** and **Height** in pixels.
* **Select and drag**: Select the element and then select one of its handles. Drag the handle until the element is your desired size.

### Position elements

There are three ways to reposition elements:

* **Specify position in pixels:** Select the element, then select the **Format** tab in the editor panel. In the **Position** section, enter your desired **X** and **Y** position in pixels. The `(0, 0)` position is at the top left corner of the page canvas and respects any configured [page margins](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/edit-report-page-setup-headers-and-footers#edit-page-setup).

* **Drag and drop**: Select the element. Drag and drop it at your desired position on the page canvas. If you want to move multiple elements at once, you can select the desired elements, and then select the (ICON) drag handle to move them as a group.

* **Using arrow keys**: Select the element and press the arrow keys on your keyboard to move the element by 1 pixel. Pressing <code>Shift</code> while pressing the arrow keys moves the element in 5 pixel increments.

## Change element layering

You can change the layering of your elements in a report. Layering refers the order of how elements appear, and whether they are on top of or behind other elements. This can be useful when you want to create more depth in your report and have elements overlap, and also when reorganizing a complex page with many elements.

To change the layer that your element appears on:

1. Select your desired element, then select ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/more.svg) **More**.
2. Select **Order**, then select your desired layering position:
   * **Bring to front**: This brings the element to the topmost layer available.
   * **Bring forward**: This brings the element forward one layer.
   * **Send backwards**: This sends the element back one layer.
   * **Send to back**: This sends the element to the backmost layer available.

## Align and distribute elements

When selecting multiple elements, you can use the alignment and distribution options available to create a clean and organized layout for your report.

1. Select multiple elements by clicking and dragging your cursor over the elements you want to select, or by pressing the <code>Shift</code> key and clicking on each element.
2. Select your desired alignment or distribution option.

   The following options edit only the alignment or distribution of options, not the size or shape of the elements:

   * **Align left**: Align selected elements by their left edge, following the X coordinate of the rightmost element.

   * **Align center**: Align selected elements horizontally by their center, using the mean of the elements' coordinates as the X coordinate.

   * **Align right**: Align selected elements by their right edge, following the X coordinate of the rightmost element.

   * **Align top**: Align selected elements by their top edge, following the Y coordinate of the topmost element.

   * **Align middle**: Align selected elements vertically by their center, using the mean of the elements' coordinates as the Y coordinate.

   * **Align bottom**: Align selected elements by their bottom edge, following the Y coordinate of the bottommost element.

   * **Distribute horizontally**: Redistribute elements to be spaced equally from left to right.

   * **Distribute vertically**: Redistribute elements to be spaced equally from top to bottom.

   The following options  change element size as well as position and alignment:

   * **Align elements horizontally**: Resize elements to fill the selection box and distribute them horizontally with equal width.

   * **Align elements vertically**: Resize elements to fill the selection box and distribute them vertically with equal height.

# Customize report settings and themes

You can also customize the look and feel of your report by editing your report’s [theme](#theme-settings) and [font](#font-settings), [color](#color-settings), [layout](#layout-settings) and [table style](#table-style-settings) settings. This document covers how to [configure your report theme and settings](#change-report-theme-and-settings).

See also [Customize element background and styles](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/customize-element-background-and-styles) for more information on customizing element padding, backgrounds, or corner sizes. To customize element size and position instead, see [Customize element size, position, and layering](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/customize-element-size-position-and-layering).

## User requirements

* You must be assigned an [account type](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/license-and-account-type-overview) with **Create, edit, and publish reports** permission. See [Account type and license overview](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/account-type-and-license-overview).
* You must enter **Edit** mode to configure the following.

## Change report theme and settings

To access report settings:

* Click the background of your report. From the side panel, select **Report settings**.

From **Settings**, you can:

* Edit your report’s theme settings, color settings and font settings to match branding and compliance standards
* Modify your layout style and layout settings to accommodate differently sized pages or screens
* Change table style settings to highlight important information

### Theme settings

Themes encompass a report’s color palette, fonts, and title and table text sizes, and are applied throughout the report once selected. Individual settings can be further modified.

You can choose a predefined theme for your report, or apply custom themes (report themes are shared across workbooks and reports). See [Create and manage workbook themes](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/create-and-manage-workbook-themes). To select a theme:

* In the **Theme** dropdown menu, select your desired theme.

### Color settings

The **Color** settings control text, button, background, element, and chart colors in a report.

<div class="table-a2 full-width header-col-200">
  | Setting                                                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
  | :-------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | **Appearance**                                            | Select between a ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/theme-light.svg) **Light** or ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/theme-dark.svg) **Dark** theme for a report.  |
  | **Theme colors > Swap preset**                            | Set a predefined color theme for report text, buttons, background, and charts.                                                                                                                                                       |
  | **Theme colors > Text**                                   | Sets the color of report text for your theme.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
  | **Theme colors > Highlight**                              | Sets the color of buttons, link text, and selection indicators in your theme.                                                                                                                                                        |
  | **Theme colors > Surface**                                | Sets the color for element backgrounds, borders, and icons in your theme.                                                                                                                                                            |
  | **Override colors > Canvas**                              | Sets a custom color for the report canvas, different from the canvas color for the theme. Select ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/x-square_clear.svg)  **Clear override** to restore the default. |
  | **Categorical colors/Sequential colors/diverging colors** | These are color schemes for the charts in your report. You can select a predefined palette or set custom colors to use for your charts.                                                                                              |
  | **Invert visualization tooltips**                         | Inverts the theme's text and background colors in tooltips.                                                                                                                                                                          |
</div>

### Font settings

The **Font** settings control fonts throughout the report.

<div class="table-a2 full-width header-col-200">
  | Setting        | Description                                                                                           |
  | :------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | **Text font**  | Sets the font for non-data report text, like element titles, element descriptions, and table headers. |
  | **Data font**  | Sets the font for report data. The default is Roboto.                                                 |
  | **Title font** | Sets the font size and color of element titles.                                                       |
</div>

Select **Revert to default** to undo your changes and reset the settings to the default. To customize text styles more granularly, see [Customize text typeface, size, and style in reports](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/customize-text-typeface-size-and-style).

The **Layout style** settings control the layout of report pages and elements.

<div class="table-a2 full-width header-col-200">
  | Setting                             | Description                                                                                                                  |
  | :---------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | **Spacing**                         | Sets the size of spacing between elements.                                                                                   |
  | **Corner**                          | Sets the shape of element corners. Choose from a square, rounded, or pill-shaped corner. The default is round.               |
  | **Data element style > Padding**    | Sets padding for a data element. Select or deselect the checkbox to add or remove padding around a data or control element.  |
  | **Data element style > Background** | Sets a custom background color for a data or control element. Set to **Auto** to match the element background for the theme. |
</div>

### Table style settings

The **Table style** settings control the format and display of tables, pivot tables, and input tables.

<div class="table-a2 full-width header-col-200">
  | Setting                 | Description                                                        |
  | :---------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | **Table style presets** | Applies a preset to configure all table style options.             |
  | **Cell spacing**        | Sets the padding around text within table cells.                   |
  | **Grid lines**          | Determines how cell borders are displayed.                         |
  | **Banding color**       | Choose a color to set as the background for alternating data rows. |
  | **Header**              | Formats table headers.                                             |
  | **Subheader**           | Formats subheaders *(applicable to pivot tables only)*.            |
  | **Cell**                | Formats data cells.                                                |
</div>

Select **Revert to default** to undo your changes and reset the settings to the default.

# Customize text typeface, size, and style in reports

When building reports in Sigma, you can customize text elements to meet your branding needs by using preset text styles, as well as more granular typeface and font sizing options.

By default, when you create a text element in a report, a default preset style is used. Reports allow you to switch between the preset style options, as well as "break" these preset styles in favor of using a custom font or size. This document covers how to [use the preset text styles available](#use-preset-text-styles) and how to [switch to more customized font options](#customize-text-typeface-and-size) if desired.

For more information on report themes and settings, like setting font throughout a report, see [Customize report settings and themes](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/customize-report-elements-settings-and-branding). * You must enter **Edit** mode to configure the following.

## Use preset text styles

By default, when you create a text element in a report, the **Medium paragraph** preset style is applied. To switch from one preset style to another preset style:

   Even when using a preset text style, you can apply other text formatting options available in the report toolbar.

If you are using a [custom text typeface and size](#customize-text-typeface-and-size) and want to switch back to using a preset style:

1. Select your text element and ensure the text is highlighted.
2. In the toolbar, select ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/link-restore.svg) **Restore style**, then select your desired preset style from the dropdown menu.

4. Enter your desired font size.

# Edit report page order, visibility, and numbers

Source: https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/edit-report-page-order-visibility-and-numbers.md

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://help.sigmacomputing.com/llms.txt

# Edit report page order, visibility, and numbers

You can reorder and rearrange your report pages, number your report pages, and change individual page visibility settings. These changes can make your report easier to navigate for users, and ensure you have control over what users see when they view the report. This document covers how to [add, rearrange, duplicate, or delete pages](#add-rearrange-duplicate-hide-or-delete-pages), [add page numbers](#add-page-numbers), and configure [page visibility settings](#configure-page-visibility).

For information on changing page setup configurations, headers, or footers, see [Edit report page setup, headers, and footers](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/edit-report-page-setup-headers-and-footers). For more information on reports in general, see [Reports overview](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/reports-overview).

## User requirements

* You must be assigned an [account type](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/license-and-account-type-overview) with **Create, edit, and publish reports** permission. See [Account type and license overview](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/account-type-and-license-overview).
* You must be in **Edit** mode.

## Add, rearrange, duplicate, or delete pages

### Add and rearrange pages

To add a new blank page:

1. Next to **Pages**, select + **Add new page**. A new page appears. The maximum number of pages in a report is 1,000.
2. To rearrange pages, drag and drop them into your desired position.

### Duplicate pages

To duplicate an existing page and all its content:

1. Next to your desired page, select ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/ellipsis-horizontal.svg) **More options**.
2. Select **Duplicate**. Another copy of your page appears.

### Delete pages

To delete a page:

1. Next to your desired page, select ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/ellipsis-horizontal.svg) **More options**.
2. Select **Delete**.

## Add page numbers

To add page numbers to your report:

1. From the **Add element** bar, select **Page number**. The page number element appears. The element automatically displays the current page number and the total number of pages in the report, in the format `x of x`.
2. To display the page number on every page, drag and drop the page number element into the header or footer. It will repeat on every page with the correct page number displayed.

<Callout icon="📘" theme="default">
  The page number element is a dynamic text element, and will be automatically adjusted to account for hidden pages when the report is exported, or when the published version is being previewed.
</Callout>

## Change page visibility

You can to hide or show pages in your report. Hidden pages are visible to the workbook owner and any user granted **Can edit** permission for the particular report can access all pages in **Edit** mode, regardless of page visibility settings. Page visibility settings apply in **View** mode only, and in report exports.

<Callout icon="🚧" theme="default">
  When a user with **Save as** permissions saves a copy of a workbook, all pages are visible in the copy, regardless of page visibility settings in the original workbook.
</Callout>

<Callout icon="🚩" theme="default">
  Page visibility is not a security feature. If you need to restrict access to data, use row-level security or column-level security instead. See [Set up row-level security](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/set-up-row-level-security) and [Configure column-level security](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/configure-column-level-security).
</Callout>

You can easily see page visibility settings for all pages in your report with the [page visibility icons](#page-visibility-icons) displayed in the **Pages** section.

You can choose to [hide pages from all users without edit permissions](#hide-or-show-pages) for that report, or [only show the page to select users and teams](#show-pages-to-select-users-and-teams).

### Page visibility icons

In the **Pages** section, display icons indicate the current page visibility setting:

|                                                                                    |                                                         |
| :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------ |
| **no icon**                                                                        | Indicates the page is visible to all users.             |
| ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/eye.svg)       | Indicates the page is visible to select users or teams. |
| ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/eye-slash.svg) | Indicates the page is hidden from all users.            |

### Hide or show pages

1. Next to your desired page, select ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/ellipsis-horizontal.svg) **More options**.
2. Select **Hide**. The page will still be visible when editing the report, but not when previewing the published version of the report or when exporting the report.

<Callout icon="📘" theme="default">
  This is equivalent to the **Hide page from all users** option when using the **Customize page visibility** functionality.
</Callout>

To show a hidden page, repeat the steps but select **Unhide**.

### Show pages to select users and teams

1. Next to your desired page, select ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/ellipsis-horizontal.svg) **More options**.
2. Select **Customize page visibility**.
3. In the **Page visibility setting** dropdown, select **Only show to select users or teams**.
4. Search for and select your desired users or teams. Select **Save**.

# Edit report page setup, headers, and footers

You can customize your report page setup (margins, orientation, size), as well as configure multiple header and footer options, to meet your reporting needs. This document covers how to configure your [page setup](#edit-page-setup) configurations and add [headers and footers](#add-and-resize-headers-and-footers).

For information on how to edit report page order, page visibility settings, and number your report pages, see [Edit report page order, visibility, and numbers](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/edit-report-page-order-visibility-and-numbers). For more information on reports in general, see [Reports overview](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/reports-overview).

## User requirements

* You must be assigned an [account type](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/license-and-account-type-overview) with **Create, edit, and publish reports** permission. See [Account type and license overview](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/account-type-and-license-overview).
* You must be in **Edit** mode.

## Edit page setup

### Change page margins, orientation and size

To change page setup:

1. Click the background of your report to open the **Settings** tab in the editor panel.
2. Expand the **Page Layout** section.
3. To change margin size, enter your desired pixel size for **Margins**. This will be applied uniformly through the upper, lower, left and right margins.
4. To change page orientation, select ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/orientation-portrait.svg) **Portrait** or ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/orientation-landscape.svg) **Landscape**.
5. To change page size, select the **Page size** dropdown and select your desired option (**A4**, **Letter**, **Legal**, **A3**, or **Custom**).
   * If you select a **Custom** page size, select your desired **Unit** from the dropdown and enter your desired page **Width** and **Height**. The maximum page size is 10,000 px in height and width.

### Show or hide page rulers

You can show or hide page rulers to help with element alignment and sizing:

1. Click the background of your report to open the **Settings** tab in the editor panel.
2. Expand the **Ruler** section.
3. Turn the **Show ruler** toggle on or off to show or hide page rulers.
4. Select **Pixels**, **Inches**, or **Centimeters** as your preferred unit of measurement.

## Create and manage headers and footers

You can [create](#create-a-new-header-or-footer) and [manage](#manage-existing-headers-and-footers) multiple headers and footers for each report. Multiple headers and footers can be [used](#apply-or-remove-headers-and-footers-on-a-page) simultaneously in a report, and can be [duplicated](#duplicate-an-existing-header-or-footer), [renamed](#rename-an-existing-header-or-footer), or [deleted](#delete-an-existing-header-or-footer) as needed.

### Create a new header or footer

To create a new header or footer:

1. Click the background of your report to open the **Report settings** panel in the editor panel.

2. Under the **Header** or **Footer** section, ensure that the **Enable header/footer** toggle is turned on.

3. In the **Header** or **Footer** section, next to  **Manage page headers/footers**, select ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/add.svg) **Add new header/footer**.
   * If this is the first header/footer in the report, you are automatically taken to the header/footer settings.
   * If this is not the first header/footer in the report, from the new header that appears under **Manage page headers**, select ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/more.svg) **More** > **Edit** to open the header/footer settings.

4. (Optional) Rename your header/footer by double-clicking its current name and entering your desired name. Press **Enter** on your keyboard.

5. (Optional) To edit the size of your header/footer, enter your desired pixel size in the **Height** field.

6. (Optional) To change the color of your header/footer, select your desired ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/fill-color.svg) **Background color** using the color picker, wheel, or palette.

7. (Optional) To upload a background for your header/footer, select **Upload image** and select an image file from the file browser. Configure your image preferences:
   * **Sizing**: Select your desired image sizing option:
     * **Shrink to fit**: Downsize the image to keep it entirely visible within the element.
     * **Scale to fit**: Expand the image to the maximum size, keeping it entirely visible within the element.
     * **Cover**: Expand the image so that the entire element is covered, even if it requires cropping.
     * **Original**: Maintain the original image dimensions regardless of the size of the element.

   * **Tile**: Turn on the **Tile** toggle to repeat the image across the header/footer until it covers the entire area.

   * Select a **Horizontal** (**Left align**, **Center align**, or **Right align**) or **Vertical** (**Top align**, **Center align**, or **Bottom align**) alignment option.

8. To apply your header/footer to a specific page, select your desired page in the Pages sidebar. In the editor panel, under **Page header** or **Page footer**, select the name of your newly created header.

9. To add elements to the header or footer, add your desired element to the report using the **Add element** bar. You can then drag and drop the element into your header or footer.

### Apply or remove headers and footers on a page

1. Scroll to your desired page, or select it in the **Pages** sidebar.
2. Under **Page header/footer**:
   * To apply a header/footer, select the name of the header/footer you want to apply.
   * To remove a header/footer, select **None**.

<Callout icon="💡" theme="default">
  After applying a header/footer, you can view all pages it is used on by selecting **Used on...** under the name of the header/footer. Select any page number to navigate to that page.
</Callout>

### Manage existing headers and footers

You can make changes to the name and appearance of your headers and footers, as well as duplicate or delete them.

#### Edit an existing header or footer

Change an existing header or footer's format settings:

1. Access the header/footer settings by either:
   * Clicking your desired header/footer on the page.
   * Under **Manage page headers/footers**, find the header/footer you want to edit, and select ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/more.svg) **More** > **Edit**.
2. Make your desired changes to the header/footer settings.

#### Rename an existing header or footer

There are two ways to rename an existing header or footer:

* While editing the header/footer, double-click its name, then enter your desired name. Press **Enter** on your keyboard.
* Under **Manage page headers/footers**, find the header/footer you want to rename, and select ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/more.svg) **More** > **Rename**. Enter your desired name, then press **Enter** on your keyboard.

#### Duplicate an existing header or footer

Duplicate an existing header or footer:

* Under **Manage page headers/footers**, find the header/footer you want to duplicate, and select ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/more.svg) **More** > **Duplicate**. A copy of the header/footer appears.

#### Delete an existing header or footer

Delete an existing header or footer:

* Under **Manage page headers/footers**, find the header/footer you want to delete, and select ![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/more.svg) **More** > **Delete**.

# Reports overview

# Reports overview

Reports allow you to make predictable, pixel-perfect, paginated exports that can be difficult to create from a [workbook](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/workbooks-overview). With reports, you can tailor exports to match compliance and branding requirements, and create precise PDFs for all your enterprise reporting needs - such as regulatory documents, invoices, order forms, and other use cases.

This document provides an overview of reports and links to additional resources.

## About reports

Reports allow you to leverage many of the same components as workbooks, and more:

* Add [data elements](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/create-a-data-element), [input tables](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/intro-to-input-tables) and [control elements](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/intro-to-control-elements) to prepare data for reporting.
* Visualize your data with [charts](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/intro-to-visualizations).
* Customize the look and feel of your reports with [UI elements](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/intro-to-ui-elements).
* Send tailored reports to the right users with [controls](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/intro-to-control-elements) and [email bursting](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/export-as-email-burst).
* Organize your analyses into distinct [numbered pages](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/edit-report-page-order-visibility-and-numbers#add-page-numbers).

## Build a report

To begin building your report:

* Create a new report: [Create and edit reports](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/create-and-edit-reports) from **Home** or from an existing report.
* Build the base of your report: [Add elements and data to a report](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/add-elements-and-data-to-a-report), such as tables, charts, and UI elements.
* Display your data clearly: [Paginate table data](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/add-elements-and-data-to-a-report#paginate-data-tables-in-a-report).
* Format and customize pages contents, setup, and branding:
  * [Edit page setup, headers, and footers](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/edit-report-page-setup-headers-and-footers) to manage page margins, size, headers, footers, and more.
  * [Edit page order, visibility, and numbers](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/edit-report-page-order-visibility-and-numbers) to manage page ordering, individual page visibility settings, and page numbers.
  * [Customize text typeface, size, and style](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/customize-text-typeface-size-and-style) to match your branding and compliance needs.
  * [Customize element size, position, and layering](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/customize-element-size-position-and-layering) to arrange and align elements precisely.
  * [Format report settings and themes](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/customize-report-elements-settings-and-branding) by editing report themes and settings.

For an end-to-end example of building a report with company branding, analytics, and bursting and export functionality, see [Tutorial: Build and export a sales report](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/tutorial-build-and-export-a-sales-report).

## Share reports

There are several available methods of sharing a report:

* [Share and export reports](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/share-and-export-reports) by downloading your report and sending ad hoc or scheduled exports.
* [Securely embed](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/create-an-embed-api-with-json-web-tokens) your report to allow users in an application or website that you own to view its content.
* [Create and edit document templates](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/create-and-edit-workbook-templates) to reuse and share reports without data. You can share these templates with [other users in your organization](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/share-workbook-templates), or [with other organizations](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/share-and-accept-cross-org-workbook-templates).

## Limitations

* Tables and input tables can be paginated up to 10,000 rows:
  * This limitation applies to how many rows are rendered in the report. All operations (like filtering, formulas, summaries, and any child element interactions) are performed on the entire dataset.
  * Report exports will display up to 10,000 rows of data per table/input table.
* Only vertical pagination of data tables is available.
* [Bursting limitations](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/export-as-email-burst#limitations) apply when exporting a report as an email burst.
* Reports do not support using warehouse views with tagged versions.
* Report pages are limited to 10,000 px in height and width.
* Each report can be up to 1,000 pages long.

# Share and export reports

# Share and export reports

This document covers how to share and export your report. For more information about reports, see [Reports overview](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/reports-overview).

## User requirements

* You must be assigned an [account type](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/license-and-account-type-overview) with the **Share documents** permission enabled.
* You must be the report owner or be granted **Can edit** [access to the document](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/folder-and-document-permissions).

## Limitations

* A maximum of 10,000 rows per table will appear in exports.
* Before exporting a report for the first time, you must publish it.
* Cross-organization sharing of reports is not yet supported.

## Share a report with other members of your organization

To invite a specific member or team to access your report:

<Callout icon="🚩" theme="default">
  When you share a document with someone, they are also granted **View** access to the data in the connection data sources.
</Callout>

1. From the document menu, select **Share and export** > **Share**.
2. Search for and enter an email address, organization member or team in Sigma you want to share your report with.
3. In the **Permission** dropdown, select your desired permission. For more information on permission options, see [Folder and document permissions](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/folder-and-document-permissions).
4. Repeat for any additional members or teams.
5. To add a message along with your report, enter a message in the **Add a message** field.
6. To send an email notification along with your report, select the **Send email** checkbox.
7. Select **Share**.

To allow general sharing of your report with users in your organization by link:

<Callout icon="🚩" theme="default">
  Guest users and external users cannot access a report shared with your organization.
</Callout>

1. In the workbook header, click **Share** (![](https://sigma-docs-screenshots.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Icons/share-user.svg)) to open the **Share Workbook** modal. You can also share a workbook from the document menu.
2. At the bottom of the modal, in the **General access link** section, toggle **Allow sharing by link**.
3. For **All members of your organization**, choose from the available permissions. The following permissions are available:
   * Can view
   * Can explore
   * Can edit After you set the permission, the workbook can be shared.
4. Click **Copy Link** to copy the link to the workbook to share with others.

## Download a report

You can download the published or draft version of a report as a PDF:

1. Open the document menu of the report, then select **Share and export** > **Export**.
2. When the **Direct download** option appears, select **Export**.

## Send or schedule report exports

You can send ad hoc exports, or schedule exports for a later time. There are multiple destinations and formats you can export a report to.

<Callout icon="🚧" theme="default">
  To export the latest version of a report, need to publish any draft changes. **Publish** your report and then **Go to published version** before exporting your report.
</Callout>

* **Email**: Send an [ad hoc email export](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/export-to-email#export-to-email-as-needed) or [schedule an email export](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/export-to-email#schedule-an-emailed-export).

* **Slack**: Send [an ad hoc notification](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/export-to-slack#send-an-ad-hoc-notification) or [schedule a Slack notification](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/export-to-slack#schedule-a-slack-notification).

* **Microsoft Teams**: Send [an ad hoc notification](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/export-to-microsoft-teams#send-an-ad-hoc-notification-to-a-microsoft-teams-channel) or [schedule a notification to a Microsoft Teams channel](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/export-to-microsoft-teams#schedule-a-notification-to-a-microsoft-teams-channel).

* **SharePoint**: Send [an ad hoc export to Microsoft SharePoint](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/export-to-microsoft-sharepoint#send-to-microsoft-sharepoint) or [schedule an export](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/export-to-microsoft-sharepoint#schedule-an-export-to-microsoft-sharepoint).

* **Google Drive**: Send [an ad hoc export to Google Drive](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/export-to-google-drive#export-to-google-drive-as-needed) as needed or [schedule an export](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/export-to-google-drive#schedule-an-export-to-google-drive).

* **Webhook**: Send [an ad hoc webhook export](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/export-to-webhook#send-an-ad-hoc-webhook-export) or [schedule a recurring export](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/export-to-webhook#schedule-a-recurring-export).

* **Email burst** (*Scheduled exports only*): Schedule [an email burst](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/sigma-computing/docs/export-as-email-burst#schedule-an-email-burst).

# Tutorial: Build and export a sales report

Source: https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/tutorial-build-and-export-a-sales-report.md

> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://help.sigmacomputing.com/llms.txt
